titulo: Hybrid light method reveals how camera signals can probe blood flow in deeper tissues
resumo: How can we efficiently collect light returning from tissues while also identifying what it tells us about blood flow in the deeper tissues? Conventional interferometric near-infrared spectroscopy (iNIRS) can distinguish signals according to the amount of time that light takes to travel through tissue, but it collects only a few photons. Camera-based systems capture many more photons, but this distinction is not realized when living tissue changes rapidly. Researchers associated with ICTER combined both approaches in a hybrid system. They showed that an appropriately analyzed camera signal can reproduce the blood-flow response observed with iNIRS for late-arriving photons, which are more sensitive to deeper tissues.

titulo: My AI agents sent emails without my OK. This simple prompt stops it
resumo: All she wanted was help from ChatGPT with her proposal, but soil hydrology researcher Ying Zhao got a lot more than she bargained for. Asking for more maps and metadata about her project—landscape restoration on the Loess Plateau in China—Zhao kept messaging “please continue” to ChatGPT for additional details. Only later did she realize that ChatGPT had taken her cue and run with it, emailing fellow researchers about her project and (politely) requesting assistance. “The responses that I received to the emails were helpful,” wrote Zhao, recounting her experience on Nature.com . “The information that I was given in these emails allowed me to advance the project. But the useful outcomes of ChatGPT’s behavior do not negate the fact that the actions it took were unauthorized.” That’s the thing about AI agents: The very qualities that make them so powerful, including initiative and persistence, also make them unpredictable and liable to doing a lot more than you anticipated. I’ve written before about how AI agents like ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, Gemini Spark, and others don’t just need prompts but outcomes . More importantly, they also require boundaries: specifics on what not to do.

The image reveals almost 63,000 radio sources, such as active galactic nuclei and star-forming galaxies, across a patch of sky about 25 times the area of the full moon. The results have been accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics. The paper is currently available on the arXiv preprint server.

titulo: Graphene networks help lithium-ion batteries store more energy and deliver more power
resumo: Making more efficient, longer-lasting lithium-ion batteries has been a challenge for researchers because adding more mass to the batteries restricts how fast electricity and lithium ions can move. To overcome this challenge, a research team has added graphene mesosponge to batteries to improve their performance during fast discharge. Their results show that graphene mesosponge is highly effective at improving the energy and power densities of commercial lithium-ion batteries.

titulo: Intel prepara mais uma linha de processadores para notebooks em 2027
resumo: A principal geração de CPUs Intel Core disponível hoje é a Panther Lake , que mescla bem eficiência e desempenho. Já a geração Wildcat Lake chegou focando em economia de energia, mas o Time Azul deve ir além com a família "Moon Lake" , com processadores formados somente por núcleos de baixo consumo (LPE-cores) e TDP baixíssimo , ao mesmo tempo em que prepara um refresh de Wildcat Lake . O grande destaque do que vem por aí, segundo o leaker Jaykihn, é o Moon Lake, projetado para suceder chips de consumo ultrabaixo como a antiga série Alder Lake-N. A arquitetura abandona completamente os núcleos de desempenho (P-Cores) e adota uma estrutura baseada em até 4 núcleos de baixo consumo, fabricados na litografia 18A padrão . Com um consumo base estimado em apenas 6 W , semelhante ao de processadores voltados para smartphones, o chip pode operar com resfriamento totalmente passivo (sem ventoinhas). Ele será montado na mesma da série Wildcat Lake (BGA1516), integrando também gráficos com a arquitetura Xe3 em um pacote compacto voltado para notebooks básicos, mini-PCs e servidores NAS de entrada. resumo: *Por Fernando Cabral A inteligência artificial está entrando em uma nova fase. Depois de ganhar espaço como ferramenta para gerar conteúdo, organizar informações e responder perguntas, ela começa a assumir um papel mais ativo nas empresas. Segundo o The State of AI 2026 da McKinsey, entre grandes organizações com receita anual superior a US$ 1 bilhão, 40% dos respondentes afirmam que suas empresas já estão escalando agentes de IA em pelo menos uma função . No ano anterior, esse percentual era de 27%. Tenho notado que setores como bens de consumo e varejo, marketing e vendas estão entre as atividades em que o uso desses agentes já é mais frequente. A tendência que observo é que esse avanço continuará nos próximos anos, como reforça uma previsão do Gartner. titulo: A carefully timed pair of light pulses can amplify the motion of atomic layers in a quantum material
resumo: The principle "Work smarter, not harder!" apparently also applies to controlling quantum materials with light. Many of their fascinating properties depend on how the atoms are arranged in the crystal. Ultrashort laser pulses can be used to alter these structures in a targeted way—the light first excites electrons, whose changed energy and dynamics exert forces on the atomic nuclei and can thereby set the atoms in motion. Such processes unfold within femtoseconds, a millionth of a billionth of a second.

resumo: A newly published study is changing our understanding of how the protein talin functions at sites where cells attach to their surroundings. The findings uncover a previously unknown mechanism by which mechanical force regulates talin, a key protein controlling cell adhesion and mechanosensing. The paper is published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

titulo: New instrument at Brazil's Sirius accelerator enables researchers to observe solar cells in operation
resumo: Scientists at the Brazilian Center for Research in Energy and Materials (CNPEM) in Campinas, São Paulo state, developed an instrument for the Sirius particle accelerator that can observe the interior of solar cells on a nanoscale while they are operating. Rather than analyzing isolated components in a laboratory setting, this new platform enables the evaluation of complete devices generating electricity under real operating conditions. It simulates daily exposure to light, heat and humidity.
